excerpt: There is something about the booming cinematic soundscapes of Caldon Glover that hits me just right. Their signature sound includes cycles of pressurization and decompression – quiet passages interrupted by brief fortissimo moments. Their latest release, The Barren Gospel, is similar in spirit but diverges in its delivery, focusing more on hushed and calmer stretches. This accumulative quality serves the album’s concept. The Barren Gospel is about a world falling into chaos and a cult-like community that promises answers but instead repeatedly manipulates the hopes of its followers. It is a structure that Glover mirrors in the music, where the calm is never quite calm. Blasts of distortion are the revelation and what they reveal is the lie. The Barren Gospel was released May 5, 2026 by Cryo Chamber. It is another must-hear from an artist who has yet to release anything that isn’t.

Meldrop is the debut release from IUGA, relying on analog and modular synthesizers to produce dark, cinematic soundscapes. Given the breadth of possibilities these devices can generate, IUGA takes full advantage and goes beyond basic drones and voltage-driven sequences. There is a hearkening back to the Berlin School in concept, but the execution is unmistakably contemporary despite vintage tooling. Across the album, IUGA favors overlapping rhythmic lines with serrated edges and granular textures – a mixture that shapes every track in different proportions. Into Your Gaze is five and a half minutes of pulsing sequences embedded in a fog. Disturbing voiceovers and field recordings drift through, punctuated by sudden swells of chords and hazy static. Aspis follows with a quieter foundation but an erratic mix of metered and unmetered passages. Toki offers thick notes that edge toward melody, the closest the album comes to lyricism. Meldrop will be released on May 28, 2026 by the Unexplained Sounds Group. It is a compelling listen.
